clusters.label: Thermoelectric effect in CuI film
clusters.definition: Thermal-to-electrical response of the CuI film, distinguished from its photovoltaic response.
clusters.reason: The evidence identifies a film thermoelectric response and explicitly distinguishes it from photovoltaic voltage enhancement.

clusters.label: Ionic-surfactant thermoelectric effect
clusters.definition: Thermoelectric effect induced by cetyltrimethylammonium chloride together with plasmonic heating.
clusters.reason: The explicit ionic-surfactant mechanism supports a distinct optothermoelectric manipulation concept.

unresolved.reason: The organohydrogel thermoelectric effect is identified only through thermal anisotropy and fire-alarm functionality; its carrier mechanism and equivalence to the other effects are unspecified.

clusters.label: Lattice strain
clusters.definition: Deformation of a crystal lattice relative to its unstrained configuration.
clusters.reason: Both denote lattice strain; material and strain origin remain properties of the respective claims.

clusters.label: Ni substitution for Co
clusters.definition: Replacement of Co atoms by Ni atoms in a crystal.
clusters.reason: Both identify the same species-specific substitution process. Host compositions, predicted site preference, and thermal effects remain separate claim details.

clusters.label: Partial filling of Sb-icosahedron voids
clusters.definition: Incomplete occupancy of Sb-icosahedron voids by filler atoms in RyMxCo4−xSb12.
clusters.reason: Both describe the same partial-occupancy condition and its associated rattling and lattice-conductivity effects.

clusters.label: Magnitude of lattice thermal conductivity reduction
clusters.definition: Amount by which lattice thermal conductivity decreases upon filling Sb-icosahedron voids.
clusters.reason: Both quantify a reduction, rather than absolute conductivity, in the same Ba/Ce/Y filling context.

clusters.label: Metallic behavior in both spin channels

clusters.label: Non-magnetic state

clusters.reason: Both use the same non-magnetic state concept in first-principles studies, whether as a comparison state or the reported material state.

clusters.label: Resistance to plastic deformation
clusters.definition: Ability of a material to resist permanent deformation.
clusters.reason: Both describe the same mechanical property; the stated elastic basis does not create a different property.

clusters.label: Crystallite size
clusters.definition: Characteristic size of crystalline domains in a material.
clusters.reason: Both denote the same structural size quantity, with doping and milling as different influencing conditions.

clusters.label: Cubic spinel structure
clusters.definition: The cubic crystal structure classified as spinel.
clusters.reason: Both labels explicitly denote a structural class, rather than asserting identity of the compositions possessing it.

clusters.label: p-Type electrical conductivity
clusters.definition: Electrical conduction characterized by hole carriers.
clusters.reason: Both report the same conduction type; compositions and carrier-density values remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Hole concentration
clusters.definition: Concentration of hole charge carriers in the studied materials.
clusters.reason: These refer to the same carrier quantity in material studies. Different dopants and directions of change do not alter the underlying quantity.

clusters.label: Hole concentration predicted by HSE calculations
clusters.definition: Hole-carrier concentration considered in the HSE investigation of Ag-doped Mg2Si.
clusters.reason: The supplied evidence explicitly frames this result as a hybrid-functional prediction, retained separately from the other material-study reports.

clusters.label: Ferromagnetic ground state

clusters.reason: Both identify the same ground-state ordering through first-principles calculations; different magnetic species remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: Reasonably good machinability

clusters.reason: Both describe the same qualitative mechanical performance in computational material studies, without specifying different machinability subtypes.

clusters.label: 100% spin polarization
clusters.definition: Complete electronic spin polarization reported in electronic-structure calculations.
clusters.reason: All explicitly report the same complete polarization value from calculations; alloy identities and magnetic contributions remain separate.

clusters.label: Minimum thermal conductivity in reported Cu2S/CuO samples
clusters.definition: The lowest thermal conductivity achieved among the reported Cu2S/CuO samples.
clusters.reason: This is a reported sample-series minimum achieved by Cu2S/20 wt% CuO.

clusters.label: Calculated minimum thermal conductivity
clusters.definition: The composition-dependent thermal conductivity minimum predicted for Yb2−xCaxCdSb2 at x = 0.3.
clusters.reason: This minimum is explicitly a first-principles prediction; agreement with experiment does not make it the same measurement concept as the other member.

clusters.label: Hydrothermal synthesis

clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify the hydrothermal synthesis method. Products and extracted roles do not change the process identity.

clusters.label: Enhanced electrical conductivity
clusters.definition: An increase in electrical conductivity relative to a reference condition.
clusters.reason: All denote increased electrical conductivity, rather than absolute conductivity or the mechanisms causing the increase.

clusters.label: Co charge compensation
clusters.definition: Charge compensation associated with Co substitution in the described Fe/Co skutterudites.
clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify Co charge compensation in Fe4−xCoxSb12-based compositions; filler chemistry and reported transport consequences remain attached to each claim.

clusters.label: Increasing Co content

clusters.reason: Both denote the same direction of change in Co substitution. Different filler compositions and resulting phase or transport effects do not change that condition.
